Uniform Title: Gorakṣaguṭikā Author: Gorakṣanātha Manuscript: NGMCP 2120 Reel Number: A62/3

Description: The *Goraksaguṭikā* (The Magic Pill of Gorakṣa) is attributed to Gorakṣa (also known as Gorakhnātha), the renowned founder of Haṭhayoga. Its colophons state that it is part of the *Kalpadrumavivekinī* and is a commentary (*vyākhyā*) on yoga. It is structured in the form of a tantra as a dialogue between Śiva and Gaurī. Although Gorakṣanātha—and by extension his followers, the Nātha Yogīs of today—was and is a yogin who should theoretically be unconcerned with ritual practice, in reality the Nātha tradition has developed an extensive liturgy centered on the worship of its gurus. This short tract contains a series of hymns (*stotra*) praising Gorakṣanātha and myths recounting their origins.
1) The first chapter (*taraṅga*) is dedicated to the birth and exploits of Gorakṣanātha. The subsequent eight chapters contain 2) the *Gorakṣadvādaśanāmastotra* and 3) the *Gorakṣakavaca*.
4) *Gorakṣahṛdaya* 5) *Gorakṣanāthakīlakoddhāraṇa* 6) *Gorakṣanāthapañcaratnastavarāja*

7) *Rakṣāṣṭakastotra* (The Hymn in Eight Verses on Protection) 8) *Gorakṣanāthāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotra* (The Hymn of One Hundred and Eight Names of Gorakṣanātha) 9) *Gorakṣanāthasahasranāmastotra* (The Hymn of One Thousand Names of Gorakṣanātha)
Notes: Revision 0: December 17, 2013. Country of Publication: India. *Śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ*.
Salutation to Śrīnātha. Pārvatī said:
"O Lord of Lords, Ocean of Mercy, I wish to hear the Saṃhitā.
O highly fortunate one, [tell me] the Saṃhitā of the great-souled Gorakṣa. (1)
How did he come to have the title "Guru," and how did he acquire the name Gorakṣa?
Whose son was this yogin, and how did his ear get cut off? (2)
"O Devaka, why do you remain silent? Do you wish to show me favor?
Speak, O Lord of the World, for the splendor of that Great-Souled One has been deposited within me. (3)
The illustrious Mahādeva said:

Oṃ. Of this *Śrī-Gorakṣanāthotpatti-kalpadruma-saṃhitā*, the great root mantra has Śrī Mahākāla as the seer (*ṛṣi*), the Śārdūlavikrīḍita meter (*chaṃdaḥ*), Śrī Gorakṣanātha as the deity (*devatā*), the nasal sound (*nāda*) as the seed-syllable (*bīja*), the staff (*daṇḍa*) as the power (*śakti*), the *kumaka* as the weapon (*astra*), and the *kolaka* as the bolt (*kīlaka*). It is employed for the fourfold purpose of attaining the desired object of one's heart.
The application is for the purpose of accomplishing the aims of human life during the recitation.
O beloved, listen to the great secret of the high-souled Gorakṣa—his state of being a Śaiva ascetic and his virtuous conduct; salutations to you, O Guru-Nātha! (4)
In a former age, when Brahmā had gone to Maṇidvīpa,
he was in the great place of Mārgāraṇya, which was indeed frequented by lions and tigers.
Their abode is established by you, O Brahmā, through great yoga;
the manifestation of Viṣṇu’s Māyā has appeared and is present before Brahmā.
A maiden named Pulocanā, who was the very embodiment of Lakṣmī herself, was seen by Viriñci; indeed, Pulocanā was of a dancing disposition.
The Creator, filled with wonder, bestowed his own daughter Damayantī upon him;
having obtained her whose seed was never in vain, that large-eyed woman became pregnant.
He conceived the embryo when the months were full,
the days complete, under auspicious lunar mansions, in a favorable month, during a bright fortnight, on an excellent lunar day, and under auspicious zodiacal signs.
A child was born to the wife of Brahmā through their union; he was the sage Viśravas, and all the birth-rites and other ceremonies were performed for him by Viśravas.
O King, by means of Brahmānanda, Sundara’s own brother became his wife;
he was named Godhana, and his daughter was Sulocanā.
From the seed of Brahmā, Maheśvarī was born to his daughter;
Viśravas, having performed the rites according to tradition, gave her the name Gorakṣī.
O Maheśvarī, just as the moon, the son of Brahmā, increases day by day during the bright fortnight, so too does the great pilgrimage of the child become attainable. 13.
O Lord of Yoga, embodiment of Yoga, son of Brahmā, O fair-faced one!
When [this] auspicious woman has obtained [you], she becomes possessed of a son and filled with great joy. (14)
Increasing day by day, he became seven years old and,
having approached his preceptor Bhārgava, indeed began his studies.
At that time, he studied the scriptures declared in the four Vedas, including all the Sāṃkhyāyana and other texts, as well as the service rendered by Gorakṣa to the preceptor’s wife.
Seeing the great wrath of his preceptor, who was intent on cutting off his ears,
the sage Viśravas then attained the state of Śramaṇa Bhārgava.
"How did my brother cut off Karna's ear while he was performing [the ritual], even though he saw his sister-in-law cutting off Karna's ear during the festival? (18)
O sage Bhārgava, how did my brother, who possesses great wrath and formidable tusks, cut off Karna’s ear while he was acting with wickedness?
O thorn of the Brahmins, you shall be reduced to ashes in an instant by my curse! 19.
Having heard the words of the son of Brahmā, Mātaṅga was overcome with grief.
O Prāṇa, hear the reason why Gorakṣa cut off his ears. (20)
Then the illustrious Gorakṣa departed, and Bhārgava abandoned [the place];
and at that spot, Gorakṣa was also made to have his ears cut off by his teacher.
I do not perform the duties of a Brahmin; I follow the way of a cowherd. As instructed by my Guru, I have undergone this remedy: the piercing of my ears and the cutting of my topknot. (22)
Having heard these words of his brothers, Viśravas departed;
after a month had passed since those events, he went to the city of Parameṣṭhin.
Jalandhara, Matsyendra, Dattātreya, and others taught the scriptures to Gorakṣa; O Supreme Śiva, [Gorakṣa] established the dharma of Gorakṣa. 24.
O lady of beautiful countenance, there were three illustrious disciples of Gorakṣa;
having personally performed the "piercing of the ears" (karṇabhaṅga), they became Gandharvas with golden-hued ears. 25.
Having played a sound upon his drum-staff, which was beautifully adorned with rubies,
he himself proceeded to praise the Supreme Brahman through knowledge.
O fair-faced one, by this method you yourself have revealed the ultimate Dharma;
the origin of Gorakṣa’s path is always recited in the Bhārata. 27.
Whether a god, a human, a yakṣa, a dānava, or a kinnara—the wise one who constantly recites this shall become like a wish-fulfilling gem and a beloved. (28)

Thus ends the first chapter, titled "The Measurement of Dharma and the Origin of Śrī Gorakṣa," within the *Gorakṣaguṭikā*, in the dialogue between Hara and Gaurī concerning the practice of yoga, in the illustrious *Kalpadrumavivekinī*.
Salutations to the illustrious Gaṇeśa.
The illustrious Mahādeva said:
Listen, O beloved, to what has been performed by me regarding the five-limbed worship and other rites of Gorakṣa; out of grace and devotion toward you, I shall recite it—behold! (1)

First, O fair-faced one, [one should cultivate] the twelve [virtues]: self-control, protection of cows, dependence upon the guru, grace, auspiciousness, the [proper] measure, and single-mindedness. (2)

Oṃ. Of this mantra of the *Śrīgorakṣanāthadvādaśanāmastotra*, the seer (*ṛṣi*) is Śrī Mahākāla, the meter (*chandaḥ*) is Anuṣṭubh, the deity (*devatā*) is Śrī Gorakṣanātha, the seed-syllable (*bīja*) is Śrī, the power (*śakti*) is Chatrahastā, and the pin (*kīlaka*) is Kurmakallola; its application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of attaining the desired objects of one's mind through the recitation (*japa*) of the twelve names.
The first is named Gorakṣa, the second is Brahmanandana;
the third is Gururūpa, and the fourth is Nādahastaka. ||3||
The fifth is the Nādapāda, and the sixth is the form of the Veda;
the seventh is the form of Bhairava, and likewise the eighth is the form of Rudra. ||4||
The ninth is Siddhirūpā, and the tenth is Chatradhāraṇa; Sundarī and Sevaka are the eleventh, O fair-faced one. (5)
Then I shall explain to you the twelfth form, which is the sandal (pādukā);
indeed, whoever recites it while maintaining their vital breath shall attain all supernatural powers (siddhi). //6//
2b) May they protect you; may they be gracious, for indeed the fulfillment of your desires shall come to pass. ||7||

Thus ends the second chapter on the Gorakṣa-guṭikā within the Śrī-Gorakṣa-dvādaśa-nāma-stotra, in the dialogue between Hara and Gaurī concerning the practice of yoga, from the Śrī-Kalpadrumavivekinī. ||2||
Salutation to the illustrious Gorakṣa.
The illustrious Pārvatī said:
O Lord, O God of gods, you are omniscient, O ocean of compassion!
How is it that the armor (kavaca) of Gorakṣanātha is the very embodiment of mantra? (1)
I wish to hear it, O Lord of the World; give the command, O Great-Minded One!
The illustrious Mahādeva said:
O lady of beautiful countenance, I bring about blessedness and a virtuous disposition.
I have revealed to you my armor, the great mantra of Gorakṣa.
Listen, O beloved daughter of the mountain; I shall indeed speak it now. (3)

Of this *Śrīgurugorakṣanātha-mahākavaca-stotra-mantra*, the seer (*ṛṣi*) is Śrī Mahākāla, the meter (*chandaḥ*) is Paṅkti, the deity (*devatā*) is Śrī Gorakṣanātha, the seed-syllable (*bīja*) is Hrīḥ, the power (*śakti*) is Śrī, and the pin (*kīlaka*) is Chatradharā. [This is employed] for the purpose of making my entire body adamantine during the recitation and chanting of the *Mahākavaca-stotra*.
The application.

Gnāṃ, salutation to the two thumbs. Gnīḥ, salutation to the two index fingers. Gnūṃ, salutation to the two middle fingers. Gnaiṃ, salutation to the two ring fingers. Gnauṃ, salutation to the two little fingers. Gnaḥ, salutation to the palms and backs of the hands. Eṣaṃ.
The ritual placement (nyāsa) of the heart and other limbs is performed in sequence.
Meditative concentration.

I bow to the venerable Guru, the Lord of Beings, Ghosts, Serpents, and Paśupati, who is the sovereign of mantras; who is accompanied by Mārga, Āpāda, Narendra, and Nāda; who bears the triple sectarian mark (tripuṇḍra) upon his forms; and who is the lord of yoga, Brahmā, Indra, and the sages, with matted locks worshipped by the king of gods. He is the eldest son of Brahmā, born from the mouth of Sāṃkṛti, and is revered by the world.
Thus ends the section on meditative concentration.
3a) The Root Mantra.
Oṃ gnū& oṃ Gorakṣanātha svāhā—this is the root mantra.
Having recited the root mantra according to one's capacity, one should perform the armor-rite (kavaca).
May Gorakṣa protect my head, and may he, in the form of the Guru, protect me;
may the Lord protect your forehead on the brow—O Śaṅkara, protect me! 4.
May the two eyes, the pair of moon-eyes, protect me and destroy obstacles;
may Ghoṭaka protect my life, and may Gorakṣa always guard me. (5)
One should protect the mouth as the Lord of Mantras, always protect the tongue as the Guru;
one should protect the ear as Mahākāla, and the sense of hearing as the form of Gorakṣa.
The Lord should always protect Maunva with Bhīmacaṇḍa-Gorakṣa;
he should protect Bāla with Raktamūrti and Śikhā with Gorakṣamūrti. (7)
May Kuṇḍala protect the fierce one, and may Kuṇḍale guard against the demon;
may Maheśvara, who has the form of Gorakṣa and the feet of a tiger, protect [us] from the scorched one. ||8||
May Ugracaṇḍa protect the chest; may Gorakṣa protect the perpetual protection;
may he in the form of Kaṅka protect the neck; and may everything be protected by the form of Gorakṣa.
May Candrabimba protect the two breasts, and Gorakṣa protect Tuṃ;
may Virūpākṣa protect the arms, and Gorakṣa protect the son of Brahmā.
Gorakṣa should protect the leaf, the merit-bestowing king of mantras;
Gorakṣa [should place] all the fingers outside, in the form of radiant energy. 11.
May the deity Namodevatā protect the nails, and Gorakṣa protect the god;
may Mahābhīma protect the navel, and Gorakṣa in the form of a water-pot (kuṇḍī). 12.
May Gorakṣa protect the belly, which is a heap of food and the very form of food;
may Gorakṣa, the Great God in the form of Yoga, protect the waist. 13.
Gorakṣa protects the *liṅga* and the form of desire, O Kāmadeva; Gorakṣa likewise protects the tresses, the intoxicated, and the insane. (14)
May the one in the form of a club protect the testicles, and likewise Gorakṣa protect the balls;
may the one in the form of a mace protect the thighs, and I, assuming the form of Gorakṣa, shall protect them. 15.
May Gorakṣa, the Lord of the Mortar, protect Ulaka and bestow happiness;
may Gorakṣa protect Dhīra, Kṣentālamūrti, and Padmatāla. ||16||
Gorakṣa [should worship] Puṇḍraka on the foot, and Hanurūpa on the ankle; Śrīdhara on the toes of the foot, and Viśvarūpa on the [other] foot. (17)
May the Moon-form protect the skin; likewise, may the Guru in the form of Fire protect the vital energy (tejas).
May he who is composed of marrow and blood protect the skin-syllable with the form of Sālva.
Maheśvara is the dense embodiment of the oceans of unstable protection;
likewise, Mahākāla, Bhairava, and Gorakṣa provide supreme protection. 19.
O beloved Muktacandreśvara, protect the child in all its limbs;
O Viṣṇurūpa, protect the wife; I salute Gorakṣa, the son of Sāmbha. 20.
O son of Brahmā, Pulomānanda, let Gorakṣa protect his son;
O wise Gorakṣa, let him himself protect his mother, father, and wife. 21.
The beautiful parasol-bearer herself should protect the path, while the attendant guards the royal gate; or else, the Guru himself, appearing in his own form, should guard it.
"May Gorakṣa provide protection for all my limbs in all undertakings.
Thus, O fair-faced one, the armor (kavaca) of Gorakṣa has been explained. 23.
O beloved Queen of the World, hear now the fruit of this armor:
those born of the three lineages—Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas—who have practiced its worship. (24)
Having fashioned this armor at the three times of day, one who writes this diagram on birch bark and wears it upon the arm will be protected by the Lord of Yogins himself.
His body would have become like a diamond, yet even the slayer of Vṛtra’s thunderbolt is not firm;
for fear of bears, tigers, and the like, he does not even hold his sword or bracelet.
His body shall become a vajra-body; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt.
Even if he dwells in the world within saṃsāra among men, gods, and kinnaras, [he remains so]. 27.
Whoever constantly recites this Gorakṣa-kavaca at the three times of the day shall become equal to one with a vajra-body amidst all destructions of fear. (28)
Indeed, they shall have no fear of weapons, nor shall there be any fear of death;
by the grace of Gorakṣa, their every desire shall surely be fulfilled. (29)
O fair-faced one, this armor of Gorakṣa was composed by me;
what more do you wish to hear regarding the Lord Gorakṣanātha? (30)

Thus ends the third chapter in the *Śrīgorakṣaguṭikā*, titled "The Armor of Gorakṣanātha," within the dialogue between Hara and Gaurī concerning the practice of yoga, as found in the *Śrīkalpadrumavivekinī*. 3.
Salutations to the illustrious Gorakṣanātha.
Śrī Pārvatī said:
O Lord, O enjoyer of the gods, how is the Gorakṣahṛdaya? How is the mantra, and how is the yantra? What state of being shall I declare to you? (1)
O Śaṅkara, I desire to hear that truth; tell it to me in detail.
How may Gorakṣa also become equal to me in honor? ||2||
The illustrious Lord said:
Listen, O beloved daughter of the mountain; with a concentrated mind, I shall explain to you the heart of Gorakṣa and its various types of yantras. (3)
O Guhyamati, listen to my words regarding that supreme vital breath which I maintain through concentration; hear it from me by virtue of your devotion and my grace. (4)
In former times, their names and so forth were proclaimed by Brahmā according to their merit; this [child], however, is the cowherd of the Great Soul (Viṣṇu). ||5||
Later, having become distressed because his ear-lobes had been severed by the preceptor Bhārgava, he [stole] this wealth of cattle belonging to the young Brahmins. (6)
The lord of the twice-born performed the protection of the master of yoga according to the prescribed rites;
for a certain time, by the turn of fate, she remained in the forest together with the herds of cows.
O son of Brahmā, when you consume poison that is equal to all [others],
and you are afflicted by that poison, you will fall under the power of the time of death.
Seeing all the cows standing in a circle around the herd, the entire multitude of cattle cried out in grief, uttering "Hā! Hā! with great intensity.
O lady of beautiful countenance, seeing Gaveṣā weeping like a corpse in the waters of the Brahmaputra,
the Ocean of Compassion appeared to her from the sky.
4b) O son of Brahmā, I likewise became a servant of the twice-born and the cows;
having entered their dead bodies, I remained there with unwavering resolve. (11)
Having seen that I had risen from my dead body, the herd of cows was delighted;
they proclaimed his name and performed their duty toward him with the herd of cows.
"Let all of you go to the house of the Lord of Yoga and lament, reaching his heart with compassion, for the sake of bringing satisfaction to the cows. (13)
O Pārvatī, I did not know that Gorakṣa had entered my body; through various illusions, I was deceived by him. 14.
"O Lord, having seen me, the lord of yogis has fallen into a state of madness;
go as you please, for this child of emotion has become insane. (15)
"What shall I do? You are ruined by worldly pleasures; go, O child, by a happy path.
Having heard this, Gaurī, with firm resolve, departed from her home. (16)
"O Brahmā, by giving me even one-tenth of a single portion from your offspring, Gaurī shall become equal to me, for Maheśvarī is my cause. (17)
Listen now to that which is the heart-essence, by performing which one becomes diligent in fashioning the armor for those sons of mine known as the twelve limbs. ||18||

Oṃ. Of this mantra known as the *Hṛdayastotra* of the illustrious Gorakṣanātha, the seer (*ṛṣi*) is Śrī Bhairava, the meter (*chandaḥ*) is Paṅkti, the deity (*devatā*) is the illustrious Gorakṣanātha, the seed-syllable (*bīja*) is Aiṃ, the power (*śakti*) is Klīṃ, and the pin (*kīlaka*) is Chatradharā. Its application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of attaining the fourfold aims of human life (*caturvidha-puruṣārtha*) through the recitation (*japa*) of the heart-mantra.

Oṃ ai& gmlvryī& to the two thumbs, namaḥ. Klī& gorakṣa glū& ṣlmī& to the two index fingers, namaḥ. Oṃ chatradharā śrī& gorakṣa guru to the two middle fingers, namaḥ. Oṃ vra& vidhinandanā dhrī& sklhī& to the two ring fingers, [namaḥ].
Homage! Oṃ, to the one who possesses other qualities, Hraṃ, to Rājeśvara, protect me, protect me!
Thphrjīṃ, homage to the two little fingers. Oṃ Aiṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ, O Gorakṣanātha, protect me, protect me! Homage to the palms and backs of the hands.
5a) Likewise for the heart-mantra and the others.
Now follows the initial meditation.

O Lord of Yogins, you who are yourself the embodiment of the lords of the senses, the protector, and the tilaka-mark; O Great Lord, you who always bear the parasol of the lineage of Tripura, the One-Eyed One; you who by your power lead Goraksha—the son of Brahma—to the state of perfection, endowed with the Vedas and the status of a Siddha, O Supreme Lord.
O Guru, protect the three great worlds! ||19||
Now, the root text.
Oṃ hriṃ hriṃ hriṃ hriṃ hriṃ! O Gorakṣanātha, paralyze the speech and the mouths of all evil-doers; protect me, protect me; grant me success, grant me success; O One-Eyed One, svāhā!
Thus ends the Gorakṣamūla.
One should utter the Praṇava, the fifth Vowel (Māyā), and the name of the deity; [then say] "paralyze all evil ones and the like with my speech, destroy, destroy! (20).
Protect yourself with the word "rakṣa," and achieve success with the wife of Vahni;
[this is] the twenty-seven-fold great mantra, consisting of numerous mantra-syllables.
O Pārvatī, I bow to Gorakṣeśvara, who consists of forty-two sections; to Śrīyantravasinī, the perfected one (siddhā), and to the form of the Guru. 22.

Having recited [the mantra] one hundred thousand times for the seed-syllable, or up to nine hundred thousand times, during the final watch of the night while seated in the deer-posture (mṛgāsana), ||23||
Accompanied by a rosary of rudrākṣa beads, the practice was performed according to the preliminary rites (puraścaraṇa) for the sake of the Guru, the Deity, and the protection of the three worlds.
For the destruction of wicked enemies and for the accomplishment of mantra-siddhi, Gorakṣa performed his sādhana according to the rules of celibacy (brahmacarya). ||25||
One should eat sacrificial food (haviṣya) and perform manual service;
the recitation of thirty-seven lakhs [of mantras] during the hours of night is the best practice. (26)
Have a pavilion constructed, provided with plantain pillars;
they shall prepare a sacrificial hall, and one should offer oblations of sesame seeds.
One should cause [the practitioner] who consumes food mixed with ghee to perform oblations of ghee;
indeed, all those who perform the recitation (japa) should offer oblations amounting to one-tenth of that number. 28.
One should perform the libation (tarpaṇa) with a tenth part of that, and likewise perform the purification (mārjana) with a tenth part of that;
O twice-born one, one should worship the daughters of Brahmā with a tenth part of that, and [conclude with] a feast for the brahmins.
Having prepared a sacrificial mound of gold, the wise Gorakṣa should draw the yantra and worship the Guru and the deity with the fivefold offerings.
One should draw a triangle, five circles, and a lotus with sixteen petals;
then, one should encircle it with four circles and four corners using the *māyā* seed-syllable.
Having fashioned four doors with sandals at the location of each door, the practitioner should always worship these Gorakṣa-yanttras. ||32||
All those who possess true wisdom should worship the Guru and the Deity with devotion;
O Gorakṣa, by means of this mantra, one shall indeed attain the desired perfection. 33.
In the midst of the eleven Rudras, O lady with the face of Rudra, one should remember this single [mantra] of Gorakṣa, which destroys the flood of all [sins]. (34)
Whatever means of accomplishment has been performed through action, word, or thought shall dissolve; it will become like a rootless tree, devoid of all sins. ||35||
The mantra of Ḍaṅkinī, joined with the six rites, is the destroyer of [all] things;
it is the annihilator of various fears and the shatterer of enemy armies. (36)
Killing, deluding, subjugation, paralyzing, and eradication—in this very sequence, O Samādhi, they shall come to pass. (37)
O Dear One, by reciting the mantra thirty-seven times, all activities— whether fire-offerings, libations, eating, or ritual purification— shall result in the perfection of the mantra.
Having first performed the worship of the King of Yantras within all objects,
he, intent upon every task, caused a pavilion to be constructed.
During the periods of *puraścaraṇa*, one should always recite [the mantra] in a deserted forest;
having attained success, one should thereafter always perform worship of you within the yantras. 40.
The offering of the bali sacrifice should be performed separately at dawn and at night;
in all ritual activities, practitioners should perform that worship with the fivefold offerings (pañcopacāra). 41.
One should offer the oblation that arises from the ritual action and perform the fire-oblation in the presence of the deity;
according to the Tantric system, O Daughter of the Mountain, this is preceded by the installation of the fire.
O Gaurī, listen in detail to the procedure for the worship of Gorakṣa in all undertakings; I shall tell you everything. 43.
At the beginning, when the rite for accomplishment has been performed, one should offer the *bali* to Ajāputra;
indeed, all eight accomplishments (*aṣṭasiddhi*) shall be attained by the practitioners. 44.
For the purpose of slaying enemies, one should offer a *bali* made of *kola* fruit;
O fair-faced lady, within three nights those groups of enemies shall meet their death. (45)

For rites concerning knowledge, causes, and effects, one should offer a ram as the sacrificial victim; for subjugation, a swan; and for the sake of prosperity, a partridge, a horn-bearer, or a peacock.
One should offer a fish as a sacrificial oblation (bali) when desiring subjugation;
for driving away [an enemy], for causing madness, and for the killing of a man, one should offer a buffalo.

When there was a desirable task to be performed, while remaining composed and healthy, he honored those esteemed according to the Vedic path with milk-rice, sweet words, and offerings of betel nut and betel leaf.
Gorakṣa is the god-guru, he who has manifested in the form of Rudra himself;
O son of Brahmā, salutations to you, the divine play of the ascetic! 49.
"Let us know the Son of Brahmā; let us meditate upon Gorakṣa;

Thus ends the sixth wave, titled "The Hymn of the Names of the King of Praises, the Five Jewels of Śrī Gorakṣanātha," within the *Gorakṣaguṭikā*— the *Śrī Gorakṣanātha-guṭikā*— in the dialogue between Hara and Gaurī concerning the practice of yoga, from the *Śrī Kalpadrumavivekinī*.
The illustrious Mahādeva said:

Oṃ. Of this mantra, the hymn in eight verses to the venerable Guru Gorakṣanātha, Śrī Bhairava is the seer (ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandaḥ), and its application (viniyoga) is for recitation and chanting for the purpose of propitiating the venerable Guru Gorakṣanātha.
Oṃ, salutations to the infinite Guru and to the delighter of Pulomā;
O Lord of Mantras, salutations to you; I bow down to the One-eyed One. ||1||
O King of Yogins, salutations to you, the Lord of the Universe and Śiva;
O Gorakṣa, who dwells with Gaurī and others, salutations again and again to you. (2)
O Nādahasta, great yogin, disciple of Bhṛgu, Maheśvara, Viśravas—homage again and again to you, to Gorakṣa, your brothers! ||3||
O Bhairava, you are the lord of the world; O Sadāśiva, you are all-pervading.
O son of Brahmā, Guru Gorakṣa, salutations to you who are the embodiment of blessedness! 4.

Salutations again and again to Brahmendra, who is attainable through meditation, whose nature is that of the Supreme Brahman and the Great Brahman, and who is the eternal abode of the lineage of yogis. ||5||
Salutations again and again to the Lord of Sacrifice, to the All-pervading One, to the Great Lord of Yoga, to Jalandhara, to Yoga, and to Gorakṣa. ||6||
Salutations to you, O Lord, who have the *ūrṇā* as your sacred thread, who bestows great liberation; salutations again and again to Gorakṣa! ||7||
Salutations to Śiva, the peaceful one, who is fond of the powers such as *aṇimā*;
salutations again and again to the Lord of the Universe, to the Universal One, and to Gorakṣa. (8)
O Pārvatī, while I am performing this *Aṣṭaka* of Gorakṣa, a man who recites it daily shall become equal to one who possesses the eight supernatural powers (*aṣṭasiddhi*). ||9||

Thus ends the seventh chapter, the Hymn of the Eightfold Protection (*rakṣāṣṭakastotra*), within the Gorakṣaguṭikā, in the dialogue between Hara and Gaurī concerning the practice of yoga, in the *Śrīkalpadrumavivekinī*. ||7||
Salutations to the illustrious Mahāguru Gorakṣa.
The illustrious Mahādeva said:
O illustrious Śailajā, by the wise Gurugorakṣa, the fruit of the five-limbed [practice] was attained intensely on the path at Mānapura, O Lord. (1)
One should attain fulfillment by reciting the hundred and eight names of Gaurī;
this hymn composed by me in five parts is for the sake of completion. ||2||
One certainly attains a fruit equal to that of the *Sahasranāma*;
it bestows the fruits desired by the mind regarding wealth, virtue, pleasure, and liberation. (3)
Various evils such as drinking liquor, slander, and violating the teacher’s bed, as well as sins like gambling and the like, will have their root in dull-wittedness. (4)
For those who speak ill of others, all [sins]— including the heinous crime of violating one's mother and even incest with one's sister—
are not as stable as the power of fire.
Truth, truth, and again truth—this [hymn] of one hundred and eight verses:
for the wise person who recites it daily, sins do not remain within his body. (6)
One seeking knowledge obtains knowledge; one seeking wealth obtains wealth;
one seeking a daughter obtains a daughter; and one seeking a wife shall obtain a wife.
O sage, one who seeks yoga attains yoga;
O fair-faced one, one who seeks a son obtains a son—this is the truth, the absolute truth. (8)
O beloved, with the eye of wisdom as instructed by the Lord of Yoga, Ekanetra, I perpetually bow down to the venerable Guru, Nātha Gorakṣa. 9.

Oṃ. Of this mantra of the hymn of one hundred and eight names of the venerable Guru Gorakṣanātha, Śrī Bhairava is the seer (ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandas), the venerable Guru Gorakṣanātha is the deity (devatā), *Śrī* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *Nāda* is the power (*śakti*), and the staff in hand is the pin (*kīlaka*). [This is recited] for the purpose of fulfilling the fruit of the recitation of the five-limbed [rite].
The application for the recitation of the hymn of one hundred and eight names, by means of the grace of the venerable Guru Gorakṣanātha. ||10||
Now follows the hymn of praise.
Gorakṣa, Gomukha, Śrīśa, Yogī, Rūpa, Sureśvara,
Brahmaputra, Mahātejas, Maṅgaleśvara, and Parvata.
O Lord Śaṅkara of the sandals, you who bear the burden of the King of Obstacles (Gaṇeśa);
O peaceful form of Śālagrāma, Lord of the Mountain, Lord of the Bull. ||11||
Padmanetra, Ekanetra, Bahunetra, Sukodara, Māneśvara, and other forms; the son of Brahmā (Viṣṇu) is the wielder of the bow. ||12||
The glorious son of Pulomā, the Lord of knowledge among knowers, Hara;
the Lord of sacrifice, the beloved of sacrifice, the king of birds, and the bearer of Umā. ||13||
Viśravas, Bhrātṛdhānya, Dhātunandana, Gaurakṣa, Pulocana, Puṇyamūrti, Puruṣottama, and Pauṇḍraka. ||14||
The paternal uncle of Paulastya, the grandfather of Aja, the brother of Kaśyapa, Nāda, the Yogin, and Gaṇya Guṇākara. ||15||
He whose banner is Garuḍa, the cowherd, the Lord of cowherds, the protector;
the crest-jewel of the perfected ones, the Lord of song, the sovereign Saṅkarṣaṇa. ||16||
The supreme Brahman, the supreme abode, the eternal Supreme Self;
the highest lord, the refuge of the world, the glorious one who bestows the fortune of Śrī upon Śrī. ||17||
The Lord of the yoga of faith, the yogi whose form is yoga, the sustainer of the earth;
he who is the form of the sun, the embodiment of meditation, adorned with crystal earrings.
14a) Richly adorned with the splendor of serpents as ornaments, the best of men is like the moon;
yet, with the dark hue of crystal earrings around his neck, he is terrifying. ||19||
The destroyer of Viśvarūpa, Kṛṣṇa, Janārdana himself, the Lord of the gods;
he whose garments are red, whose form is red, whose eyes are red, the Lord of the Kula. ||20||
Candranātha, Somanātha, Viśvātmā, Viśvanāthaka;
Bhuktinātha, Muktinātha, Naranātha, Narāntaka. ||21||
With a protruding belly, long arms, long eyes, and a long navel;
with a lolling tongue and a parasol in his hand, he resembles a beautiful servant. ||22||
O fair-faced one, the wise person who recites this hymn of one hundred and eight verses to Gorakṣa—this "One Hundred and Eight Verses to Gorakṣa"—[attains the fruit]. (23)
At the end, one is liberated from all sins and becomes a wish-fulfilling gem, O beloved;
having enjoyed happiness in this world, one shall attain the city of liberation at the end. ||24||

Thus ends the eighth chapter, the hymn of one hundred and eight names of Śrī Gorakṣanātha, for the purpose of completing the five limbs of the practice of yoga, within the dialogue between Hara and Gaurī concerning the practice of yoga in the *Śrī Kalpadrumavivekinī*, specifically regarding the *Gorakṣaguṭikā*. 8.
Salutations to the illustrious Guru Gorakṣanātha.
Pārvatī said:
O Lord of Lords, ocean of mercy, protector of the world, save me!
I always bow down and offer salutations to You, the Lord, the Master of Yoga, the Sovereign. (1)
I shall hear the great mantra of Gorakṣa from the words of Bhava;
first the hymn on his origin, and secondly the one called the twelve [verses]. (2)
The third is its armor (kavaca), the fourth is likewise the heart (hṛdaya);
the fifth is the entire ritual of worship, exposition, and so forth, as well as the pinning (kīlaka).
And the sixth is the most wonderful King of Hymns (*Stavarāja*) beginning with the "Five Jewels" (*Pañcaratna*);
and the seventh is the *Aṣṭaka* hymn, O Śaṅkara, through your grace. (4)
For the purpose of completing the five limbs, listen to the one hundred and eight names; indeed, know that this eighth [chapter] contains all mantras and tantras. (5)
O Benefactor of the World, although you have understood all the yantras and other such matters,
I wish to hear again the compendium (saṃhitā) concerning Gorakṣanātha.
How was the Thousand Names proclaimed, and how was the hymn of praise uttered?
O Lord, ocean of compassion, tell me everything; I wish to hear it, O Master. (7)
The illustrious Mahārudra said:
"O fawn-eyed one, you speak of blessedness arising from meritorious deeds;
indeed, I shall tell you everything regarding the mantras and other teachings of Gorakṣanātha. (8)
First, O Maheśānī, hear [the account] of the birth of the practice of yoga;
afterwards, I shall now proclaim your thousand names.
On that very ground where the arising of the practice of yoga occurs,
the Mother of the World shines resplendent on Maṇidvīpa in the ancient aeon.
Our counsel was revealed at the end by those who had accomplished their task;
they brought back that most wonderful celestial chariot, the Puṣpaka.
O Goddess, by me also was I created, joined with Brahmā and Viṣṇu;
in due time, you shall attain the form of a creeper in heaven, reaching a place devoid of water. 12.
I am the one who beholds ten million cosmic eggs; I am ten million Brahmās;
I am ten million Viṣṇus; and I am indeed that true, unshakable mountain.
O lady of beautiful countenance, in the past, having gone to the world of the gods where many wonders were to be seen, I beheld a great marvel, just as Brahmā and Viṣṇu did.
Abounding in the beauty of great sprouts and joined with flowers and blue lotuses, it was endowed with various trees and adorned by various ponds. ||15||
15a) In that delightful place, frequented by hosts of apsarases with various magnificent ornaments,
there were great sounds of singing and instrumental music, along with many dances performed by excellent women. ||16||

"O Gauri, having seen all these wonders from this celestial chariot, you have attained a state of amazement, even though we remain here with our asceticism, which is difficult for others to endure and established through gentle perseverance. (17)
With lions, tigers, and elephants that had been trained for turning back and performing tasks,
and with deer and other animals engaged in playful sports, they were deep in their fondness for dancing.
Deprived of the company of enemies and of various enjoyments, the man dwells in various places with groups of seekers of liberation and throngs of sages emaciated by austerity.
He perceived cats playing with mice, Garuḍas with serpents and other creatures,
and Rākṣasas with humans— all engaged in delightful play together.

O Great Wonder, behold! Having gone during the night to the rivers flowing from the Ocean of Nectar, such as the Amatsya and others, you saw the waters and the fires merged together in their seats. 21.
Celestial chariots, which pierce the vital points, are seen by us departing from our presence;
and through the eye of knowledge, the couple perceive supreme bliss in due time.
It was covered with leaves that were exceedingly beautiful, extending for a hundred yojanas, and provided with enjoyments such as jewels and gems situated upon the sandy grounds. ||23||
The sky was made fragrant by winds carrying various scents, while the oceans, acting as friends, constantly formed rows of mechanical devices and other structures upon its surface.
It was strewn with swans and *kāraṇḍava* ducks, beautified by ruddy geese and other birds,
and served as a dwelling for peacock plumage, made lovely by the immediate rising of the moon.
Behold, O you two, the splendor brought from the celestial chariot;
at those times, the chariot moves with swift speed according to the rule.
At the time when those three of ours— the Aṣṭakas— entered into splendor,
[they were endowed] with the totality of all splendor, becoming beautiful and well-adorned. (15b) 27.
Beautiful, lovely, rich in splendor, she manifested herself as Pramamaṅkā. ||28||
The female form and the name Yoga belong to the male through practice;
from this, one maiden and one youth were manifested as splendor. (29)
O Gaurī, Brahmā, the self-born four-faced one, said:
"Go there to that great, beautiful, and most splendid grove. (30)
Just as Brahmā and Viṣṇu are adorned with various groups of women of many different colors, so too are the feet of my Goddess Śaṅkarī. ||31||
They stood upon the throne at the feet of Sadāśiva,
situated above that king of yantras which was shaped like a wheel.
The Mother of the Universe, the Large-eyed One, the Mistress of the World, the Great Sovereign. ||32||
O beloved, O sovereign of all castes, show us at once this celestial chariot; we shall quickly ascend it and remain situated upon the northern part of the earth. 33.
A woman may become fair-complexioned (Gaurī) and composed of Brahmā and Viṣṇu;
she attains a great wonder through the contrary and universal velocity [of the breath]. 34.
And having gone there, they served the Goddess, the Mother of the Universe;
at that time of great delusion, the three attained the Great Service. (35)
"What should be done by the people of the world? [There are] the Bhairavas such as Asitāṅga and others.
In a previous kalpa, there was a son of Brahmā named Gorakṣa. (36)
Likewise, for me, who am preceded by my portion, the Goddess shall be the bearer of the parasol;
she stands as a new woman in the world, surrounded by a multitude of other women.
But Mātrā alone would be Viśvamātā; in the practice of yoga, she remains like one who has become silent, having come and stood upon the ground like a staff. ||38||
16a) If the Sovereign of the World, the Mother of the Universe, perceives one's practice of yoga and acts of devotion,
then she, the Mother, becomes pleased with great speed. (39)
With sweet warbling like that of cuckoos, he addressed him with words that enchanted his senses:
"O Lord of Yoga, go wherever you please as you wish. (40)
The triad of the fourth Guru—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara—are the portions of that Guru; why then do you praise them separately in Sāketa? 41.
With Bhīṣma and Droṇa at their head, and Aśvatthāman and Vikarṇa [following], Yudhiṣṭhira is the great vessel, and Vasudeva is the Lord of the Gods. 42.
Thus the gods, though empowered, were deluded by the practice of yoga;
first, the knowledge of lineage was attained through the concentration of yogic practice. 43.
Therefore, O best of gods, go; you shall obtain worship equal to that of my own shoulder.
For in both the stationary and the moving, the stability of all things exists through speed. 44.
"O children, those two deer-eyed ones shall become renowned throughout the world";
having thus granted this boon for the practice of yoga, the Mistress of the Universe [departed]. (45)

Having heard these words, the Mother of the World, the Sovereign of the Universe, departed from the city and performed penance according to the prescribed rites, absorbed in the practice of yoga. (46)
O Maheśvarī, O Mistress of Yoga, O Mother of the World who stands before us, that Māyā which is the cause of the non-entry into the lineage is [your power]. 47.
At that time, Gorakṣa granted boons to us as well:
"O Brahmā, O Mahāviṣṇu, O Lord of the World, O Maheśvara! (48)
"O Rudra, who embodies the form of Time, resort to the feet of the Mother of the World!
Having heard these words of Gorakṣa, [he was surrounded] by us, by women, and by the Gaṇas. (49)
Gorakṣa regards that which is deliberated upon by the mind as heavy;
listen, O Lokeśvarī, for by that [deliberation] Brahmā and Viṣṇu were created by me. (50)
16b) The great hymn of Gorakṣa, known as the *Sahasranāma*;
the two most excellent ones with parasols in their hands, the great ministers of Bhuvaneśvarī. (51)
For the sake of accomplishing the task for the sake of the universe, and for the granting of great liberation,
[he spoke] regarding the events at the beginning of the previous kalpa and the renowned bestowals of boons.
Śrī Gorakṣa said:
Listen, O beloved Mahādeva, you who are the cause of creation, preservation, and destruction;
in a previous kalpa, you were manifested by the Blessed Lady through her form.
You are Brahmā for all the worlds; by me, too, you have been revealed as such.
You are Viṣṇu, the performer of the acts of creation and protection for all. (54)
O Rudra, you are eternally the performer of the act of destruction for all the worlds;
and you are Gāyatrī, Sāvitrī, Sarasvatī, and so forth by name.
By the grace of the Blessed One, they all attain devotion;
having performed the work of creation, maintenance, and destruction, they reach the end of time. (56)
Even Brahmā is subject to the power of time, and Viṣṇu as well is constantly so;
and you too, O Lord Mahādeva, must come under the sway of time. (57)
At that very moment, the skin of the Brahmā of the previous kalpa was torn away;
then, by wearing that divine Brahmā-skin as a garment, he attained divinity.
Then Brahmā, assuming the form of a headless trunk (kabandha), restored life once more;
he made his own feet the feet for them, and they became a group of beings intent on their duties.
O Viṣṇu, you must always perform meditation through this artifice;
having assumed the form of a Vetāla, go to where the Lord of the Gods is seen.
Mahādeva, the Lord of Beings, became manifest as the Lord of Forms;
he was always served at the back by Bhuvaneśvarī.
In the Śrīkalpa, you, the master of every kalpa, shone forth as the beginning of all activity;
Bhūtas, Ākabaṃdhas, Vetālas, and the Mātṛs themselves became your servants.
All the powers, beginning with Indra, become subject to her; what need is there to speak further?
For she, the sovereign of the world of the virtuous, desires creation again in the blink of an eye.
Formerly, in a previous kalpa, I was the son of Brahmā named Gorakṣa;
you were Rudra, you were Brahmā, and you were Viṣṇu during these two kalpas.
"By the grace of the Blessed One, I am a son who is free from old age and death;
but you three gods are deluded by the delusion of the world. (65)
"O Brahmā, O Viṣṇu, O Śiva, I know nothing of the events of the past;
in this city of Maṇidvipa, the Lord of the Gods resides. (66)

"Perform service to the Mother of the World; grant me your grace and accept [this offering]. Though you have attained the state of womanhood, you shall once again become the illuminator of the world. (67)
"Your power has been attained; the Mistress of the World is pleased.
Having heard these words of Gorakṣa, the Daughter of the Mountain [spoke]. (68)
Again Brahmā spoke these words to Gorakṣa:
"Listen, O large-eyed one, to the word of Brahmā, O lady of beautiful countenance. (69)
The venerable Brahmā said:
O illustrious Gorakṣa, you are blessed with the eyes of a deer;
formerly, you were the wise son of Meghakalpa. (70)
"O son, Gorakṣa is seizing our very consciousness;
at such times as these, what am I not well aware of? (71)
"O father, tell me the means for the service of the Sovereign of the World;
for I am dull-witted and my nature is that of a woman—how may I serve so that Śrī may be pleased? (72)
Mahādeva said:
Having heard the words of the venerable Brahmā, he spoke the words of Gorakṣa:
"Listen, O fawn-eyed one, to how Gorakṣa has spoken. (73)
Śrī Gorakṣa said:
O Brahmā, O Hara, O Viṣṇu, you man, listen to my words:
in kalpa after kalpa, that woman comes into my presence as a man.
Thirty-seven lakhs of koṭis of mental aggregates have passed away.
O fortunate one, there is no doubt that even in this kalpa, a man who hears this teaching ten times will become a creator of the world; listen, O Vidhātṛ!
O fair-faced one, I gave the single-syllable mantra of Jaganmātṛ along with three groups; through that connection, you obtained the mantra of Guru Gorakṣa.
I have been meditated upon by these three for as many years as there were in the past;
I know Gaurī, and I am known even by Brahmā. (79)
"Know that even Viṣṇu was previously intent upon knowing [this]";
having understood this, Gaurī then [attained] the five Śrī-Gorakṣas. (80)
The Great Goddess composed this hymn of a thousand names for me;
O Gaurī, listen now to the thousand names of Gorakṣa in detail. (81)
It begins with the letter *ka* and ends with the letter *kṣa*, joined with various mantras;
subsequently, the names are filled in from the vowel *a* to the vowel *a*. (82)
Kaṅkālakālarudra, O Kṛṣṇa, whose own form is *krīṃ krīṃ*;
Kālokāla, Khaṇḍakalpāṇa, and Kalpakeśvara. ||83||
Kīrtimanta, Kīrtimān, Kīrtibhairava, and Kīrtika; he who is the embodiment of the *kiṃkāra* mantra, and the creator of the *krīṃkāra* mantra. ||84||
The one residing in the seed-syllable *krīṃ* has the form of a black cobra (*kālasarpa*);
and the one residing on Mount Kara has the form of Mount Kara. ||85||
O Lord, you are the master of the lineage, renowned as Karagaṇa;
you are the Kulācārya, the upholder of the Kula, and the sustainer of the Kula, just as you are. 86.
He whose form is the principal mountain (Kulaśaila), who holds the peak at the end of the Kula;
18a) the Lord of Kalās, the Lord of Time (Kālanātha), the Lord of Kula, and the Lord of the Sky (Khaleśvara). ||87||
Those who destroy the wicked, those with swords in hand, and likewise those bearing the khaṭvāṅga staff;
those whose essential nature is the seed-syllable *khiṃ khiṃ*, and those who proclaim the seed-syllable *khriṃ*. ||88||
The bearer of the void, the lord of the wicked, the protector of the void, and the ender of the void;
the syllable "kha," the abode in the sky, the master of the sky, and the destroyer of the wicked. ||89||
He whose crest is the sky, who is the lord of the sky, and the destroyer of the sky;
he whose form is the sky, whose hair is the sky, whose eyes are the sky, and whose face is the sky. 90.
O Khaṇḍa, O Khaṇḍakhaṇḍamūrti, O you whose very nature is the Khaṇḍacakra;
O Khaṇḍanātha, O Khūranātha, O Khūreśvara, O Khurādhipa! ||91||
O Gurugorakṣa, Gonātha, Gopāla, Gaugaveśvara;
O Go-netra, Gaṇanātha, Dhagaṇendra, Gaṇanāyaka! 92.
Lord of the Gaṇas, Teacher of the Gaṇas, Sovereign of the Gaṇas, Lord of Virtues;
whose essential nature is the seed-syllable *gnīṃ*, and who proclaims *gnīṃ* as the seed-syllable. ||93||
Gayānātha, Gayākāra, Gayeśvara, Gayādhara, the embodiment of the Gayā-piṇḍa, and the illuminator of the demon Gayāsura. ||94||
Gayāsura, Viṣāda, Gandhamādanagandharūpaka, Gandheśvara, Gandhavāha, Gandhamādana, and Gośira. (94)
Lord of the fortress, consumer of the fortress, Lord of poison, the Gaṅgaka;
Lord of the Gaṅgā, King of the Gaṅgā, the ocean of the Gaṅgā, the ender of the hosts. ||96||
The light of all branches of knowledge, the illuminator of all branches of knowledge;
he who holds a bell in his hand, whose ears are like bells, whose form is the bell, and the Lord of the jar (Ghaṭeśvara). ||97||
O you who dwell in the jar, O lord of jars; oṃ ghi, ghi—those who reside within the seed-syllables!
O you of dense syllables, O teacher of dense [wisdom], O lord of density, O ender of density! ||98||
Ghanasyāma, Ghanāṅkāra, Ghanāntaka, Ghavargaka;
dweller on Mount Ghaṭa, Ghaṭoghni, and Gāvarasaka. ||99||
The word "ghaṭa" (pot), light, the syllable "ghaṭa," the pot, happiness, the sun, knowledge, the syllable "ghoṃ," the sun, and likewise splendor— these are all [associated with] Ghaṭa. ||100||
The ṅa-group has Ṅakara as its lord; it has the form of the seed-syllable Ṅaṃ.
Ṅe is the form of the Rāṅga-potaṅa, and Ṅa is the maker of the mountain Ṭa. ||101||
Ṅaṭeśvara, ending with the letter Ṅa, Ṅamukhī, and likewise Ṅalinan;
Ṅasimākarṇakāra, and Karṇaphāṭaka by means of the form. 102.
The leather-clad one, the wearer of skin, the wanderer upon skins, the unmoving and the moving;
Caṇḍikā, the Lord of Caṇḍikā, the fierce one, and the slayer of the fierce. ||103||

The fierce-eyed one, the one who strikes down, the one with eyes as flickering as the moon, the one with trembling limbs, the one whose head is the moon, and the skillful one who bears the moon upon his crest. 104.
Caturānana, Sūtra, Catureśa, Campaka, the illustrious Campakeśvara, Campanātha, and Arvaka. ||105||
Ciṃbīja, Carmapāṇa, and likewise Carmakāreśvara;
Chinnamastāpati, Chaṇḍa, Chaṇḍeya, and Chaṇḍanāyaka. ||106||
Chaṇḍanātha, the letter Cha, Chalinī, Chyā, Chaleśvara, Chalanātha, Chala, Keśa, Chaṇḍabheda, and Chalonmana. (107)
Chalavidyā, Chalasamjñā, Chalabheda, and Chedaka;
Chedakarna, Chedamūrti, Chaḍaiśvara, and likewise Charin. ||108||
O you who hold a parasol in your hand, O bearer of the parasol, O leader of the lords of parasols;
O lord of the parasol, O dweller in the parasol, O creator of the mountain of the parasol! ||109||
He who assumes the guise of a sneezer, he who destroys the night-dwellers in disguised form;
O Lord of Waters, you who take the form of water at the hands of the daughter of Jayantī and the sage! 110.
The lord of waters, the source of water, who possesses water;
he who is born from prayer, the husband of his wife, the lord of his wife, and the bringer of victory. ||111||
Lord of Flames, garlanded with flames, Master of Flames, Lord of Recitation;
born from the bearer of the garland of victory, he is the destroyer of the birth of those blind by birth.

The giver of birth and the lord of beings, the conquerable and the unconquerable, whose nature is the syllable Ja; the Lord of Japa, the one who is the syllable Jīṃ, and the dweller on the mountain of Japa. ||113||
The Lord of the insentient, the destroyer of the insentient, the one who takes away the knowledge of the insentient;
he who is perfected by people, and the servant of the husband of Janaka’s daughter. ||114||
Jhapamālā, Jhalajhaṃlā, Jhaṃkeśvara, and likewise Jhaṣa; Jhapamāna, Jhiṃkāra, and Jhīṃkāra, who proclaim the seed-syllable (bīja). ||115||
And the multitude of demons, leaping up, made a loud "jhama" sound. ||116||
Jhakka, Jhaṃpa, O Lord of Pārvatī, you who are the source of the seed-syllables of the *jha*-group. ||117||
Jhañña dwells upon the mountain; Jhīṃ is the one who makes the sound "jhikāra" and causes trembling.
Jhalana is the form of purification, while Jhāpera is the embodiment of the Jhāṭi form. ||118||
Jhaṣeśvara, the syllable Jha, Jhamāntaka, Jakārikā, Ñameñcara, Ñamo, and the proclaimer of the seed-syllable Ñaṃtatrakāra. (119)
Ñaṃ is the form of the seed-syllable, Śrīnātha, Ñanteśvara, and Ñameśvara; Ñaṃ is the form of Vagaru, Ñatṛkānta, Tatrīmālā, and Ñasāsika. ||20||
The proclaimer of the letter Ṭa, the Lord of the Ṭikaṭīkas, the Lord of Ṭala, Ṭaṅkeśvara, the letter Ṭi, Ṭiṭṭibha, and whose nature is the seed-syllable. ||121||
Ṭala, the dweller of the mountain; Ṭapomukha; Ṭipākara;
Ṭaṅkanātha; Ṭaṅkakeśa; Ṭaṅkalocana; Paṭaka. ||122||
The Lord who destroys the city of death, the one who delights in the ṭamaru drum;
the Lord of Ṭāmara, the protector of the ṭopa, whose name resounds with the sound of the ṭāṅkāra.

Lord of the short task, wielder of the short blade, lord of the short trunk and the short-tusked one; lord of the short trunk, lord of the short spear, eye of the staff, and lord of the syllable *ṭa*. ||124||
The lord of the land of Tuṇḍa, likewise the sovereign of the Tuṇḍa country;
the sound of the letter Ṭa, the resonance of Ṭāṃ, the Ṭakapālas, and Tāraka. (125)
Ṭuṅkeśvara, Ṭuṅkanātha, Ṭaṅkeśa, and likewise Ṭaruṇa;
Ṭaruṇeśvara, Ṭāruṇika, and Ṭāraka, the destroyer of Tripura. ||126||
19b) Lord of the barren soil and the non-barren soil, Lord of the barren soil, subduer of *ṭhāma*;
he whose form is *ṭhuṇa*, whose face is *ṭhuṇa*, Lord of *ṭhumala*, the *ṭhākura*. ||27||
Ṭhālāpati, Ṭhulanātha, and likewise Ṭhulakeśeśvara;
Sthitimūrti, Sthiramukha, Sthalāvāsa, and Sthaleśvara. ||28||
Rudra resides at Sthalanātha, as do Caturānana, Āsara, Daṇḍimukha, Ḍamaruka, and likewise Taḍamaruvallabha. (129)
Sthūlākāra, Sthūlamukha, Ḍambunātha, Ḍapākara, Ḍapānātha, Ḍāmarika, Ḍalanāyaka, and Ḍuṇḍubha. (130)
Ḍiṃ and ḍiṃ are indeed the Lord of Seeds (Bījeśvara), while hrīṃ and hrīṃ are the very nature of the Seed-syllables.
Ḍhrīṃ is the seed-syllable, ḍhu is the syllable cha, and ḍhuṃ is Ḍhumāra, the Lord of Ḍhala. ||131||
Dharanātha, Dhasaṃjñā, Ḍhaṃkanātha, Ḍhimākara, Ḍhimeśa, Ḍhamakāra, and he whose essential nature is the sound "Ḍhuṃ Ḍhuṃ. ||132||
Ḍharāntaka, Ḍhālarūpa, Ḍhaḍhārūpa, Ḍharīmukha, Ḍhārāḍhīreśvara, and Ḍhatulānāḍhalaneśvara. ||133||
He who is the sky of the ocean of the letters ṇa, śa, bha, ra, pa, ṇa, ma, ṇa, da, ga, and ṇa;
he who is the lotus-stalk of the ṇa-lotus, the sound, the one whose command is sound, and likewise the Lord of Sound.
He who dwells in the seed-vessel of the dramatic performance, he who resides in the Talātala hell,
he whose form is splendor, he whose bed is splendor, and likewise the Lord of the Bed.
O youthful son of the Sun, O destroyer of the darkness of ignorance, O Lord of splendor, O Lord of brilliance, O Lord of youth, O you who perform the cosmic dance! ||136||
He has the form of a young boat and possesses the beauty of a youth;
he is the embodiment of the palmyra tree and the manifester of the sound "tāla. ||137||
He dwells on Mount Tala like the lord of Tala;
he is the form of the seed-syllable *Trīṃ* and possesses the channel of the sound *Trīṃ*. ||138||
The slayer of the demon Tāraka, the savior of Tāraka’s lord, whose deeds are saving, whose nature is the essence of liberation, the Lord of Tripura, and the master of the Tantras. 139.
Lord of Tripura, whose nature is protection, who holds the triple umbrella;
sovereign of the Tripura mountain, lord of the Tripura mountain. (140)
He dwells in the abode of Tripura, he is a servant of the goddess Tripurā,
and he is the end of the Asuras of Tripura— just as the male practitioner of Tantra is to the female practitioner of Tantra.
O Lord of Tantra, whose form is Tantra, the slayer of the demon Tanka; O Lord of Tantra, who consists of Tantra, and likewise the Lord who protects through Tantra. ||142||
Talpa-paya-talpanātha, Talpakānta-taleśvara, Thalavāsa, Thalakarṇa, Thālī, and he who is established as Thālādi. ||143||
Thālī, Pṛya, Thaṃtha, Śabda, Tha, Tha, Varṇeśvara, as well as Dāmarī, Damara, Udāma, Dīmodara, and Dayākara. ||44||
The upholder of compassion, beloved of compassion, the subduer, the belly of the deceitful; the curiosity of the self-controlled, the vessel, and the crusher of the demon Damana. ||145||
He is the flower of the *damanaka*, the beloved of Kadamañjati, the Lord, the terrible one, the sovereign of the terrible, the lord of giving, and the embodiment of generosity. (146)

He is the very nature of the merit of giving, the bearer of the banner of Dharma, the one who upholds the earth, the embodiment of the stream [of compassion], the beloved of the earth, the one who maintains all things, and the bearer of the burden. ||147||
The Lord of those who bear the burden, the steadfast one, the Lord of Wealth in the form of intellect;
Dhanvantari, the Lord of meditation, the Lord of meditation, and the destroyer of obstacles. ||148||
Lord of Dharma, embodiment of Dharma, bearer of the earth of sound;
Lord of the earth, blessed soul, righteous one, master of the wheel of Dharma. ||149||
The blessed one, whose form is as precious as a guru, the blessed lord, the ender of wealth;
the delight of men, the king of men, he who is in human form, and the banner of kings. ||150||
The embodiment of drama, Lord of dance, Lord of men, Sovereign of men; the blue one who provides protection to men, Lord of the blue, and the ender of men. ||151||
O brother of Nīlakānta, O kinsman of Yamarāja;
O full moon, O one of full splendor, O Lord of the Full, O Lord of the Full Moon. ||152||
Padmanābha, Padmanātha, Padmākṣa, Padmarūpaka; the destroyer of heretics and sinners, Parvata, and Pārvatīpati. 153.
20b) With noose in hand and the form of Palā, likewise Pāśin and Pāśeśvara;
fond of the vessel, the bearer of the vessel, the vessel itself, and the one whose nature is the vessel. ||54||
O Beloved One, O You of lovely form, O Lord of the beloved, O Destroyer of Palāśa trees;
O Wearer of yellow garments, O Yellow One, You who are the very embodiment of a son. ||155||
The Lord of Pauṇḍra, Puṇḍrarūpa, Puṇḍarīkākṣa, Pāṇini, Pātakī, Khaṇḍarūpa, and the bestower of boons upon the Pāṇḍavas. (56)
Lord of the Pāṇḍavas, protector of the Pāṇḍus, Lord of the Phakiras and Phakires;
Lord of the Phatkiras, the Phikhaṇḍa, the one seated upon the plow (Phālāsana), and likewise Phaṇḍa. ||157||
The proclaimer of the seed-syllable *phrīṃ*, the Lord of Seeds, the bestower of strength, the maker of strength, the Lord of Strength, the Lord of Power, and the Leader (*vināyaka*). ||158||
You are Bindurūpa, Bindāvidyādhipa, Vidyādhara, Virūpākṣa, Viṣṇu, and likewise Vimala. ||159||
Viśeṣāt, Vaiśyarūpa, Vaiśyanātha, Viḍambara, Bileśvara, Bilvapriya, Bilāsa, and Varuṇeśvara. ||160||
The husband of a courtesan, the embodiment of the Vedas, the beloved of Vāruṇī, the one from Pṛthvīhika; the protector of children, the lord of the young, and the destroyer of Bala. ||161||
Vīramūrti is intoxicated by strength; Vāgmatī is the embodiment of water;
Bāṇanātha is the subduer whose hand holds an arrow. 162.
The Lord of Subjugation, the one who takes the form of destruction and obstacles;
likewise, the Lord of Wind, whose form is wind, and the destroyer of wind. ||163||
Bhagaṃdhara, Bhagākāra, Bhaganātha, and Bhairava; Bheṣīdhara, Bheṣinātha, Bheṣīrakṣaka, and Bhilla. ||164||
O beloved of Bharuṇī, O brother, O lord of Bharuṇīs, and likewise O brother;
O Mahākāla, O Mahārudra, O Mahādeva, O Manu, O Maṇi! (165)
O jewel-necked one, O pride of the mind, O beloved of proud women, O pearl-like one;
O great lord, O great-eyed one, O great knower of the Vedas, O great asura! ||166||
21a) Muktamālā, Mokṣarūpa, Mokṣajvālā, Narādhipa, Palāpalāṃdhipaya, Janātha, and Yameśvara. ||167||
The lord of the *rala* forest, the master of the chariot of the *rala*-lord, the bearer of the *rala* that draws the chariot, and the one whose hands are adorned with *rala* ornaments. (168)
Lord of the beloved of Ramā, Sovereign of Kings, the quality of passion (rajas);
dweller on Mount Rajaparvata and the one who fashioned Mount Rajaparvata. 169.
O Lord of Kings in the form of a monarch, O Protector of the Night, O You whose face is like the wind;
O Lord of the assembly of women, O Destroyer of the pride of the Lord of Laṅkā. ||70||
Lord of modesty, with hanging crest, with hanging wisdom, maker of speech; embodiment of speech, lord of the suspended, lover of parched grain, maker of the *laṭhā* sound. ||171||
The destroyer of Laṭeśvara, Lambamukha, and the demon Lambāsura;
he who is intensely devoted to the forest, the earth, and the sound of the *āmāra* bird. 172.
Śeṣamūrti, Śeṣanātha, Śeṣeśvara, Śaśāṅka;
Śaktisiddhi, Siddhinātha, Śileśvara, Simākara. ||173||

The seed-syllable *ṣi*, the *ṣaluga* [note], the *gāndhāra*, the end of *ṣa*, the one afflicted by *ṣāna*, the lord of *ṣaga*, the thief of the union of *ṣaṃ*, the face of *ṣasī*, and the lord of *ṣala*. ||174||
Sālva, Sālvapati, Śānta, Śāntanātha, Śaśīdhara, Śaśinetra, Śaśimukha, Śāmba, and likewise Śāmbheśvara. (175)

The Lord of Śrī, whose face is auspicious, the husband of the Mother of Fortune, the Lord of the primordial sound, the embodiment of those who have sought refuge, and the protector of those who have come for shelter. ||176||
Halī, Halimukha, Hāla, Hāleśvara, Hayomukha; Hayanātha, Hayajñāna, Hayārī, and Nāśahāṭaka. ||177||
Hāṭakeśvara, Hrīṃkāra, Hatyāmocana, Hālana; Hetopadeśa, Hetu, Hetukāraka, and Hiṃkara. ||178||
The essential nature of the *hiṃ* syllable is the cause of dwelling within the *hrīḥ* seed-syllable;
he is the friend of Hanumān, the companion of the fire-oblation (*homa*), and the very embodiment of the oblation itself. ||179||
He has tawny eyes, he is golden-hued, his flesh is tawny, and his face is tawny;
he is a portion of Hara, he possesses the form of Hara, he is the Lord of Hari, and he is the maker of the horse-sacrifice.
O Rūpanetra, Hanumān, Lord of the Haras, Lord of the Monkeys;
O Lord of the Hālās, O Destroyer of those slain by Hāla, O Lord of Haṭha! ||181||
Heramba, Hanu, Gandharva, Halisādhipa, Harimaya, Hanana, Hāni-rūpa, Haṭamūrti, and Halāyudha. ||182||

The Knower of the Field, the Producer of the Field, the Lord of the Field, the Crusher of the Kṣatra; He whose form is the saline essence, the Uprholder of the Kṣatra, and the Concealer of the Leader of the Kṣatra. ||183||

He whose form is the field, the lord of the kṣatra, the lord of the field of patience, the lord of the night, the lord of forgiveness, the lord of the field, and whose face is like the tip of an arrow. ||184||
Kṣātradharmaprakāśa, Kṣātradharmanāyaka, Kṣaurakarmeśvara, Kṣaura, Kṣauragandharva, and Kṣemaja. (185)
He dwells upon the mountain of the kṣatriyas and is the creator of that mountain of the kṣatriyas;
he has the form of one who crushes the kṣatriyas and possesses the essential nature of the wrath of the kṣatriyas. ||186||
He has the form of the blood of the Kṣatriyas and possesses the essential nature of the strength of the Kṣatriyas;
he is the ripening of the mantras of the Kṣatriyas, the one who diminishes [all things], and the one who brings about destruction. ||187||
The destroyer of the kṣatriyas and the illuminator of kṣatriya-knowledge;
the one whose nature is the salty ocean and whose nature is the vigor of the kṣatriyas. ||188||
O Lord of Forgiveness, Lord of the Kṣatriyas, Protector of the Kṣatriyas, Maker of Night;
O Lord of the Maker of Night, Shaver of the Small, Treasure-Trove of Dharma and Patience. 189.
He is the very nature of the Kṣatriya’s weapon and likewise the lord of the Kṣatriya’s life;
he is the form of the milk from which the butter is extracted, and likewise the one who assumes a diminished form.
Aryamā is the one who has overcome the enemy and is the destroyer of foes;
he is the illuminator of the host of enemies, the female enemy, and the Lord of Aruṇā. ||191||
Atrīvasaprakāśa, Ayonijaprakāśaka, Abjanandana, Asthi, Asthika, Svara, and Atrija. ||192||
Anumata, Atrika, Atrinatha, Ayomukha, Agni, Agnajanman, Arkamaṇḍala, and Arkaja. ||193||
He is the very essence of the sun’s splendor and the illuminator of the solar mantra;
he is Arkanātha, Arka, Aṃśa, Āditya, and the primordial form. ||194||
Ādijñāna, Ādinātha, Ārtikeśvara, and Agnigā; Ādideva, Ādiyogī, Ādeśa, and Ārtakāntaka. ||195||
Āliṅgana, Āruṇisa, Ānandeśvara, Āntara; Ādilokeśvara, Ālī, and Āsīviṣasvarūpaka. ||196||
He was the wearer of ornaments, and he was the illuminator of knowledge;
he was the lord of the ten directions, and likewise the Lord of the Form of Hope.
Āśānātha, Āgnahika, Āgnaheśvara, Hatyaka—these are the teachers of wicked form; [then] Duṣṭāgraha and Haleśvara. (198)
Ilāvṛtanivāsa, Ilānātha, Ilāntaka, Ilāmārgaprakāśa, Iṣṭeśvara, and Imānidhi. (199)
Thus he is the illuminator of sound and the very nature of history;
thus he is the nature of fragrance and the dweller in his own abode. ||200||
Thus, he is the form of the mantra *ili*, the Lord of the *liṅga*, the Indriya;
he is the form of Indra, the Lord of Indra, the Lord of Indra, and the Consort of Umā. (201)
Umākānta, Umānātha, Umāniṣi, Umākara, Ugranātha, Ugreśa, Ugrācārya, and Umāsaja. ||202||
Umeśvara, Uttarēśa, the dweller in the northern region (Uttarākhaṇḍa), the one in the form of a bull (utrī), the source of origin (utpattika), Utpattēśvara, and Ugraja. ||203||
Ugratārāsevaka, Ūgraparvatakāraka, Ugrasenasutāhaṃtī, Ugracandra, and likewise Ṛtu. (204)
The king of seasons, the lover of seasons, the one dear to seasonal flowers, as well as the distributor of seasonal knowledge, and likewise the lord of mantras in the season. ||205||
Kinsman of the seasons, lover of the seasons, dwelling near the Lord of the seasons;
Rantideva, beloved of the seasons, possessing the vigor of the seasons, whose nature is the essence of the seasons. ||206||
Ṛryamā and Ḷmārga, Laṅkeśa the slayer of life;
she whose form is the seed-syllable Ḷ, and he whose form consists of the Ḷ-group of letters. ||207||
The essence of the *ḷṃ-nātha-rāsa* is truth; he is the very form of the mantra *rā rā maṃ*.
He is the syllable *aiṃ*, the speech of obeisance (*aiṃ namaḥ*), and the dweller on Mount Aiṃdraparvata. ||208||
Oṇḍrapuṣpa, Priyakara, Odravartika—Oṃ, homage!
You who dwell on Mount Odra and whose very nature is the Odra-vidyā. ||209||
Āṭaghāta, Omama, Otṛ, Oturvidyā, Svarūpaka; Oturnātha, Otukara, Odrukānta, Ogaṃdhala. ||210||
Audyānavāsin, Oṃkāra, Auṃ, Vidyā, Ausama, Nidhi, Autigaṃdhāvatī, Autya, and Aucaparvatavāsaka. ||211||
From the science of the Asura Aurva came Aurvakaṇṭhi and Aṭeśvara;
likewise from Aurvatejas came Aulī, Aulīndhara, and Dhara. (212)
Auliṅganātha, Auliṅga, Auliṅgeśvara, Śrīpati;
the Lord of the Asuras and of the egg-born, the auspicious Lord of the Egg (Aṇḍeśvara). ||213||
Antakeśvara is the form of Aṅkanātha-Antakeśvara;
he is the end-maker, the syllable Aṃ, the seed-syllable Aṃ, and the one whose nature is the interior. ||214||
The destroyer of the demon Aṃtra, the sustainer of the celestial parasol,
he whose abode is the seed-syllable Aṃ, situated within the interior of the cosmic egg.
He is named Aṇḍamātama, whose form is the letter *a*;
he is the embodiment of the world below (*atala*), the Lord of *atala*, and the one who moves downward. ||216||
He dwells within the circle of fire, he has the form of the circle of fire;
he is the very nature of the luster of fire, and he has the form of the pillar of fire. ||217||
Aśvavāha, Aśvaśiras, Aśvalocana, Antika; Aduputra, Adupati, Aśleṣāpati, and Abidha. ||218||
O you of great form and great eyes, another arm is the Tandava dance;
you are the Yaksha, the Lord of Yakshas, the goal, and the embodiment of the ford of ignorance. ||219||
The Lord, whose form was rendered powerless by the arrow of the Bhilla, became known by the name Gorakṣanātha among the outcastes; thus ends the one hundred and twentieth [chapter].
O Pārvatī, this supreme hymn of a thousand names of Gorakṣa, which has been composed by us, is indeed difficult for even yogīs to obtain.
O wise Gorakṣa, may you be pleased with this intelligent one who constantly recites [this] for those with passion, those free from passion, and for yogins living as householders. 222.
The supreme hymn of a thousand names is endowed with a thousand virtues, joined with a thousand forms of knowledge, and possessed of a thousand perfections. ||223||
O Goddess of a thousand faces, when joined with a thousand sciences,
she becomes a wish-fulfilling gem that brings joy to her devotees.
He becomes equal to Gorakṣa, a revealer of various mantras;
O Maheśvarī, he recites it three times daily at the three junctions of the day. (225)
On the lunar festivals of the moon and sun, the contact and release [of breath] are recited;
O Brahmin, the practitioners have performed the count of the movements and offered me food. (226)
Thus, O beloved, the limbs of Gorakṣanātha have been fulfilled;
may the illustrious Gorakṣa be gracious to us and be seen by us with the three eyes. 227.
Thereafter, Bhuvaneśī, being pleased, bestows success as her guest-gift.

Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled "The Thousand-Name Hymn of Śrī Gorakṣanātha," within the Gorakṣa-guṭikā, concerning the practice of yoga in the dialogue between Hara and Gaurī, from the *Śrī Kalpadrumavivekinī*. 9.
